items.title: Dave Liebman — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: A tune that me and Mac – that Mac’s on one of the records with – from the ’90s, Port Ligat

ctx.x: I played a class of mine the chart that McNeely wrote for you on Sing, Sing, Sing last spring. They loved it, because it’s such a perversion of the original.

And the exchanges. The record we just did – it’s Quest for Freedom, we were talking about – that we did with the band from Frankfurt, the HR, Hessian Rundfunk, their area big band, like the Cologne band, McNeely, me, and Richie. This is a heavy record. A Sunnyside release that nobody knows about. It’s too bad. It came out in

September. The writing and the playing – he did – he took my heavy tunes. He took a couple of Richie’s, but he really took mine, W[TC], World Trade Center, the deep harmonic tunes that only McNeely understands. He’s the only arranger. [Vince] Mendoza, to a certain degree. [Bill] Dobbins, to a certain degree. But Mac is – Mac knows what me and Richie play. A tune that me and Mac – that Mac’s on one of the records with – from the ’90s, Port Ligat, he took that, Pendulum, the tune Richie always – we always played…
